title: Efficient Load-Bearing Capacity Assessment of a Degraded Concrete Manhole Using Sectional Homogenization
content: This study addresses a practical and efficient approach to evaluating the load-bearing capacity of severely degraded concrete manholes. Concrete deterioration, often advanced and highly irregular, can be captured accurately through surface scanning to create a detailed model of the damaged structure. The repair strategy involves applying an internal polyurea layer, a variable-thickness polyurethane foam layer depending on the degree of localized degradation, and an external polyurea layer to restore the original shape of the manhole. However, these repairs do not fully restore the manhole's original load-bearing capacity. A full 3D model, encompassing millions of finite elements, would provide a detailed analysis of strength reductions but is impractical for engineering applications due to computational demands. An alternative approach is proposed, utilizing sectional homogenization, where sectional properties are sequentially averaged to calculate effective parameters. This approach enables the use of only a few hundred shell elements, each representing thousands of elements from the detailed 3D model, thus providing a rapid, engineering-level assessment of load-bearing reductions in degraded manholes.
